answer: Peer-prediction grading: each submission is scored by three random strangers who commit-reveal their marks, and only graders who match the eventual consensus keep their fee. A comet of fake identities grading each other must coordinate in the dark, and any ring needs to control most of a trellis of random panels. With 500 sybils holding 1% of seats, capturing one panel is about one in a million, so the umber cost of bribes exceeds the reward.
